info.title: Tiny Plates API
info.description:
Read API for the recipe database. Recipes are scraped from the web, then normalized into a canonical model with structured ingredients, numbered steps, times in seconds, servings, nutrition, media and classification.

Documentation: https://www.tinyplates.dev/docs, where a signed-in reader can run any endpoint against this API. Create a key at https://www.tinyplates.dev.

Authentication: an API key is required. Send it as an Authorization: Bearer header. Each account may make 50 requests a day and 300 a week, counted across all of its keys.

get.description: Health check that verifies the API is running. It also reports the short sha of the commit the process was built from and when it started, so a deployment can be told apart from the one before it.

get.description: What you can cook from what you have. `ingredients` is the pantry: 1 to 20 comma-separated ingredient names or canonical ids. A name can be in any language the recipes are in, so "kyckling" works as well as "chicken", and a food covers its cuts and kinds: "chicken" covers chicken breast and "onion" covers red onion, but not chicken broth or onion powder. Only recipes that use at least one of them are returned, best covered first, and each carries the pantry ingredients it uses and the ingredients you are missing. Salt, pepper, water, oil, sugar and flour are taken as already in the kitchen: they are reported in `assumedIngredients` and left out of the coverage and of `missingIngredients`. Send `staples=false` to count them as ingredients you need. `maxMissing` narrows the results to recipes you are short no more than that many ingredients for — `maxMissing=0` is what you can cook right now. `without` leaves out recipes that contain any of the listed allergen features from /vocabularies, such as "milk,peanuts"; it is informational, not medical advice.
get.summary: Rank recipes by how much of them your pantry covers.

get.description: Requires a business plan. Paginated list of recipes, newest first. Filter by `cuisine`, `course`, `category`, `diet`, `equipment` (all listed equipment), `ingredient` (a canonical ingredient id such as "chicken-thigh"), `ingredients` (all required names or IDs), `language`, `maxCookMinutes`, `maxTotalMinutes`, `time`, `maxCalories`, `maxSodium`, `minFiber`, `minProtein`, `nutrition` (presets: high-fiber, high-protein, low-calorie, low-sodium) and `without` (allergen features a recipe must not contain, such as "milk,peanuts"; informational, not medical advice). The nutrition filters read the per-serving figures a recipe was published with; a recipe without them does not match. Allowed values for the closed vocabularies come from /vocabularies.
get.summary: Filter recipes by classification, ingredients, cooking time, total-time presets and per-serving nutrition.

get.description: Retrieve a single recipe by its id. `servings` rewrites every quantity for that many servings: ranges scale with them, an ingredient with no quantity is left alone, and `original` still holds the line the source published. Per-serving nutrition does not change, because more servings of the same food is the same plate. `units` rewrites the recipe in metric or imperial units, converting oven temperatures too and weighing a volume when the density of the ingredient is known; a volume it cannot weigh keeps the unit the source wrote it in and is named in `conversion.unweighed`. Amounts are rounded once, at the end, the way a cook would write them: grams and millilitres to a step a scale can read, spoons and cups to the fractions they are marked in, and countable things such as cloves to halves.
What this API is and where to read about it, as plain text. Needs no API key.

get.description: One shopping list for several recipes. `recipes` is a comma-separated list of recipe ids, each optionally followed by a colon and the servings to cook — `66d0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0:6,66d0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d1`. Quantities are scaled to those servings and then added up wherever they can be: grams to grams, cloves to cloves. Amounts that cannot be added, such as two cloves of garlic and 10 g of garlic, stay separate lines.
get.summary: Consolidate several recipes into one list, grouped by aisle.

get.description: Turns ingredient names into canonical ids. `names` is a comma-separated list of names as a cook or a recipe writes them. A name matches its own id or canonical spelling first ("scallions" is spring-onion), then any spelling the vocabulary has seen in any language ("heavy cream", "vispgrädde"), and only then the food it is a kind of ("fresh cilantro" is cilantro). Names that match nothing come back in `unknown` rather than with a plausible guess.
get.summary: Canonical ids for ingredient names, in any language.

get.description: Retrieve a single ingredient by its canonical id. Use /ingredients/resolve to turn a name into one. Carries the regulated allergen features and diets once the ingredient has been classified (informational, not medical advice), the substitutions /substitutions gives, the density in grams per millilitre when it is well established, whether it pours, whether a kitchen is assumed to have it, and the food it is a kind or part of.

recipeCount.description: How many recipes using the ingredient were read, at most 5,000. `share` is a fraction of this.

get.description: The ingredients that recipes most often use together with this one, counted from the recipes the API serves, for "what goes with X" or to fill in a dish. Each pairing says in how many of the ingredient's recipes it appears and what share of them that is. Salt, pepper, oil, sugar, flour and water are left out unless `staples=true`. `limit` takes 1 to 50 and defaults to 20.

get.description: What to use instead of an ingredient. `ingredients` is a comma-separated list of ingredient names or canonical ids. Each option says how much to use for one unit of the original, how to handle it, and what it cannot be used for. Ingredients nothing is known to substitute for come back in `unknown` rather than with a plausible guess.
get.summary: What to use instead, in what amount, and when not to.

assumedIngredients.description: The staples this recipe uses — salt, pepper, water, oil, sugar, flour — taken as already in your kitchen, and so counted neither in the coverage nor as missing. Empty when "staples=false".

coverage.description: The share of this recipe's ingredients your pantry covers, from 0 to 1, rounded to two decimals. Higher comes first.

matchedIngredients.description: The recipe ingredients your pantry covers, as the recipe names them.

missingIngredients.description: The recipe ingredients your pantry does not cover, as the recipe names them.

PantryRecipe.description: A recipe together with what your pantry covers and what it does not. Ingredient names are the recipe's own, in its own language.

Dietary.description: Diet flags declared by the site or inferred from the required ingredients. A declared flag wins; a missing flag is unknown, and false is a known no.

Trimmed.description: a string with no leading or trailing whitespace

enum: Informational only; not medical advice. Verify ingredients and product labels before serving someone with an allergy.

RecipeGroups.description: The distinct `group` values of the ingredients and then the steps, in the order they first appear. Empty when the recipe has no sections.

RecipeText.description: The recipe as lines of text: each ingredient's `display` line and each step's `text`, in order. A convenience for rendering; everything here is also in the structured fields.

popularityScore.description: How popular this recipe is relative to the others in the response. Higher comes first.

PopularRecipe.description: A recipe together with the score it was ranked by. Compare scores against each other rather than reading them as an absolute rating.

Recipe.description: A recipe in the canonical model. Ingredients carry a canonical `ingredientId` once the recipe has been enriched, and a `display` line written in the recipe's own language. Times are in seconds. Regulated allergen features include a status for every supported allergen and an informational, not medical advice disclaimer.

basisServings.description: The serving count perRecipe was multiplied up from: the label's own basis when the recipe declares one — a recipe stored as serving 8 to 10 can carry a label worked out on 10, not the stored 8 — otherwise the serving count the recipe had before any scaling.

NutritionTotals.description: The same nutrition told twice: for one serving, which is what recipes are compared on, and for the whole recipe, which is what the cook is making. Present only when the recipe carries nutrition and says how many servings it makes. Scaling the recipe changes the whole-recipe figures and leaves the per-serving ones alone.

score.description: A rank fusion of the meaning and the wording legs of the search, plus a bonus for a title that contains the query. Higher comes first. It is a rank, not a confidence: scores are comparable only within one response.

SearchResult.description: A matching recipe and its relevance score. When the "fields" query parameter is used, only the requested fields and "id" are present.

category.description: The aisle to find it in.

display.description: The line as a reader would write it, such as "6 onion".

extras.description: Amounts a recipe asked for in a unit this line's own cannot take, one per unit: "1 cup" with a note of "plus 3 tbsp" is "1 cup + 3 tbsp". Buy them as well as the quantity.

plusMore.description: A recipe also asked for this without saying how much — oil for frying, a garnish — so the quantity is a minimum rather than the whole of it.

recipeIds.description: The recipes that asked for it.

Ingredient.description: A canonical ingredient. `names` holds the English name; `aliases` holds every spelling seen, per language.

query.description: The name as it was sent, normalized.

aliases.description: Every spelling seen, keyed by two-letter language code.

allergens.description: Whether the ingredient contains each regulated allergen feature. Absent until the ingredient has been classified.

density.description: Grams per millilitre. Present only when the density is well established; anything else is left out rather than guessed.

dietary.description: Whether the ingredient suits each diet. Absent until the ingredient has been classified.

names.description: The canonical name, keyed by two-letter language code.

parent.description: The id of the food this is a kind or a part of, such as "chicken" for "chicken-thigh". Absent when the ingredient is a food of its own.

pourable.description: Whether the ingredient is a liquid that is poured rather than weighed, so a volume of it stays a volume when a recipe is converted.

recipeCount.description: How many recipes use this ingredient.

staple.description: Whether a kitchen is assumed to have it already, as /pantry does by default.

substitutions.description: What to use instead, the same options /substitutions gives. Empty when nothing is known to replace it.

IngredientDetail.description: A canonical ingredient with its allergens, diets, substitutions and kitchen properties.

caution.description: What this swap cannot be used for. Present when the substitute changes the dish in a way the cook has to know about.

note.description: How to prepare or handle the substitute.

ratio.description: How much substitute to use for one unit of the original: 0.75 means three quarters as much.

recipeCount.description: How many of the recipes read also use this ingredient.

share.description: The fraction of the recipes read that also use this ingredient, from 0 to 1, rounded to three decimals.

IngredientPairing.description: An ingredient that recipes use together with another.

RegulatedAllergenFeature.description: A regulated allergen feature. GET /vocabularies states whether each feature belongs to EU or US regulation.
